executive_assessment.text: Historical assessments identify Dry Corridor agricultural dependence and named high-vulnerability departments, alongside metropolitan flood and landslide exposure.
The 2019 SIPRI/WFP research describes drought, weak cohesion and gang restrictions on programme participation; these are local historical mechanisms, not a current national climate–violence estimate.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024 reports: The assessment places 73% of districts in high-drought zones, concentrated in high-poverty Usulután, Ahuachapán, Cabañas and La Unión departments.

Source dated 2025 reports: The 2025 NDC says 88.7% of national territory faces disaster risk; Cabañas, Morazán and Ahuachapán have high vulnerability combining socioeconomic factors, weak basic-service access and environmental stress.

Source dated 2019-11 reports: The study reports that gang dynamics required WFP to negotiate program access and beneficiaries to obtain permission to participate; field visits included San Miguel, Uluazapa, Jiquilisco, Ozatlán, Usulután, Suchitoto, Agua Caliente and San Salvador.

Source dated 2018-02 reports: The assessment ranks San Salvador, Soyapango, Ilopango and Cuscatancingo as most vulnerable to heavy-rain flooding and landslides; San Salvador recorded 209 floods and 79 landslides during 1960–2015.

Source dated 2018-02 reports: During three years of rainfall anomalies, maize and sorghum yields fell 43% and bean yields 29% in La Unión and Morazán; over 90% of producers used maize-bean-sorghum systems.

known_gaps.text: The sources do not establish a climate cause of gang violence; the 2024 World Bank statement is explicitly conditional, while the SIPRI/WFP nexus description is a qualitative 2019 context analysis.
No current subnational assessment was found showing how insecurity constrains climate-adaptation implementation in 2026; SIPRI/WFP program-access observations date to 2019.
The 2023 Climate-Fragility Risk Brief PDF exceeded direct retrieval limits and was not used; the WFP Central American Dry Corridor report PDF returned 403 and only its landing page was opened.
March 2019 gang and programme-access findings are historical; they do not describe the materially different 2026 security context.
Field-visit municipalities are not assigned identical gang restrictions. No source establishes that drought caused gang formation or measures a climate-attributable violence rate.
